description: This course covers the fundamentals of computer organization and architecture, including instruction set architecture, processor design, memory hierarchy, and input/output systems. Topics include the design and implementation of arithmetic logic units, instruction decoding and execution, pipelining techniques, cache memory organization, virtual memory management, and system interconnects. The course also explores modern architectures such as RISC-V, ARM, and x86, along with standards like PCI Express and USB 3.0. Students will study algorithms for memory management, such, as page replacement and cache replacement policies, and examine the role of operating systems in managing hardware resources. Specific technologies like assembly language programming, microprocessor design, and system-on-chip (SoC) architectures are also covered.

clos.text: Define the key components of a computer system, including the CPU, memory, and I/O devices, and describe their interconnections using the von Neumann architecture.
Explain the principles of instruction set architecture, including addressing modes, data types, and control flow, using examples from RISC-V and x86 architectures.
Apply pipelining techniques to optimize instruction execution and analyze the impact of pipeline hazards on processor performance.
Implement a simple memory hierarchy, including cache and virtual memory systems, using algorithms for page replacement and cache replacement policies.
Design a basic computer system using system-on-chip (SoC) architectures and evaluate the trade-offs between different processor architectures in terms of performance and power consumption.
